scenario.topic: Pick the technology stack for a new community web platform

options.name: MERN Stack (MongoDB, Express, React, Node.js)
options.upside: Offers full JavaScript stack with a large ecosystem and reusable code between client and server.
options.concern: May require additional configuration for complex data relationships and transactions.

options.name: Django with React Frontend
options.upside: Provides a robust backend with built-in admin and security features alongside a flexible React frontend.
options.concern: Requires managing two different languages and frameworks, increasing integration complexity.

options.name: Ruby on Rails with Hotwire
options.upside: Includes built-in real-time features and convention-over-configuration for faster development.
options.concern: Smaller developer community compared to JavaScript-based stacks.

options.name: Serverless Stack with AWS Lambda and Vue.js
options.upside: Scales automatically with usage and reduces server management overhead.
options.concern: May introduce complexity in debugging and cold start latency.

shared_context: A group of seven developers is selecting a technology stack for a new community web platform that must support user profiles, real-time chat, and content sharing. The stack should be maintainable, scalable, and have an active developer community.

personas.name: Maya
personas.background: Full-stack developer with a passion for rapid prototyping and real-time features.
personas.private_goal: Choose a stack that accelerates development with built-in real-time support.

A.reason_for: Full JavaScript stack allows code reuse between client and server.
A.reason_against: May require extra work for complex data relationships compared to Rails.

B.reason_for: Robust backend with security and admin features complements React frontend well.
B.reason_against: Managing two languages and frameworks adds integration complexity.

C.reason_for: Built-in real-time support and convention-over-configuration speed up development.

D.reason_for: Automatic scaling is attractive for future growth.
D.reason_against: Serverless complexity and cold start latency could slow development.

personas.name: Liam
personas.background: Backend engineer focused on maintainability and scalable architecture.
personas.private_goal: Select a stack that balances scalability with developer community support.

A.reason_for: Large ecosystem and JavaScript consistency across stack aid maintainability.
A.reason_against: Complex transactions might be harder to implement.

B.reason_for: Django's robustness and PostgreSQL backend are reliable for scaling.
B.reason_against: Mixing Python and JavaScript increases complexity.

C.reason_for: Rails' built-in real-time features and conventions improve productivity.

D.reason_for: Serverless scaling is ideal but debugging challenges concern me.
D.reason_against: Cold start latency and complexity may hurt user experience.

personas.name: Nina
personas.background: Frontend-focused developer with experience integrating React with various backends.
personas.private_goal: Ensure the frontend-backend integration is smooth and manageable.

A.reason_for: Single language stack simplifies frontend-backend interaction.
A.reason_against: MongoDB's handling of complex relations is less ideal.

B.reason_for: Django backend with React frontend offers a solid, secure foundation.

C.reason_for: Rails with Hotwire offers real-time features but less React familiarity.
C.reason_against: Smaller community and different frontend approach may slow iteration.

D.reason_for: Vue.js frontend is appealing but serverless backend adds complexity.
D.reason_against: Debugging and cold starts could disrupt development flow.

personas.name: Omar
personas.background: Cloud engineer experienced in serverless architectures and modern frontend frameworks.
personas.private_goal: Leverage serverless benefits to minimize infrastructure management.

A.reason_for: Node.js backend with React frontend is familiar and flexible.
A.reason_against: May require more manual scaling and server management.

B.reason_for: Django backend is robust but less cloud-native than serverless.

C.reason_for: Rails offers real-time but less suited for serverless scalability.
C.reason_against: Smaller community and traditional hosting model limit cloud benefits.

D.reason_for: Serverless stack scales automatically and reduces operational overhead.

personas.name: Zara
personas.background: Junior developer interested in modern JavaScript frameworks and cloud technologies.
personas.private_goal: Work with a modern, scalable stack that supports quick iteration.

A.reason_for: Full JavaScript stack is easy to learn and widely used.
A.reason_against: Complex data handling might be tricky.

B.reason_for: Django backend is solid but mixing languages is harder for me.

C.reason_for: Rails is mature but less trendy and smaller community.
C.reason_against: Less familiar language and frontend tech.

D.reason_for: Serverless with Vue.js is modern and scales well without much ops.

personas.name: Eli
personas.background: Experienced JavaScript developer focused on maintainable and reusable code.
personas.private_goal: Maximize code reuse and leverage a large developer ecosystem.

A.reason_for: Full JavaScript stack allows sharing code and has a large ecosystem.

B.reason_for: Django backend is robust and secure, with React frontend flexibility.

C.reason_for: Built-in real-time is nice but Ruby is less familiar and smaller community.
C.reason_against: Less code reuse with Ruby and Hotwire.

D.reason_for: Serverless scaling is good but debugging and cold starts are drawbacks.

personas.name: Tara
personas.background: Backend developer with a focus on security and data integrity.
personas.private_goal: Ensure the backend is secure, reliable, and supports complex data well.

A.reason_for: JavaScript stack is flexible and widely supported.
A.reason_against: MongoDB may struggle with complex data relationships.

B.reason_for: Django with PostgreSQL offers strong security and data integrity.

C.reason_for: Rails has real-time features but smaller community and less security focus.
C.reason_against: Ruby and Hotwire are less familiar.

D.reason_for: Serverless scaling is attractive but debugging and latency are concerns.
D.reason_against: Cold starts and complexity reduce reliability.
